title: SiliconFlow Pricing: Model Costs Per Token (2026)
summary: SiliconFlow pricing is pay-per-token with no flat plan. Determine your costs using model rates and learn the rate limits for your account.
body_markdown:
## Every SiliconFlow model priced per million tokens


On the figures confirmed here, SiliconFlow's flagship text models **charge $4.40 to $13.50 per million output tokens** , and its image models charge $0.005 to $0.06 per image, so the model you select significantly determines your per-unit cost.


The model you pick moves the bill more than anything else.


For generation-heavy work, output tokens are the metered unit that dominates cost, so the flagship ranking is on output price.[Sovyron](https://sovyron.com/providers/siliconflow/) 's[SiliconFlow listing](https://sovyron.com/providers/siliconflow/) puts the three flagships here.

### Flagship model price gaps on SiliconFlow


Kimi K3 costs about three times what GLM-5.3 does. **At 50 million output tokens a month** , that's $675 against $220, a $455 gap before you have tested whether the quality difference matters for your task.


### SiliconFlow price spread within one model family


Within one vendor's line the spread is just as wide. On[SiliconFlow's pricing page](https://www.siliconflow.com/zh/pricing) , Qwen3.5-9B is $0.15 per million output tokens, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is $1.80, Qwen3.5-122B is $2.08, Qwen3.6-27B is $3.20 and Qwen3.8-2.4T is $6.


A classification or extraction job that the 9B model handles shouldn't run on the largest one, because the top of that range **costs 40 times the bottom** . The 122B model costs only about 16% more than the 35B-A3B, which makes that step easy to test.


### Image models


Image models **charge per image, not per token** . On[SiliconFlow's pricing page](https://www.siliconflow.com/pricing) , Z-Image-Turbo is $0.005 per image, FLUX.2 pro is $0.03 and FLUX.2 flex is $0.06.


$5, $30 or $60 buys a thousand images, a twelvefold spread, meaning your monthly budget determines which models you can afford. Draft or bulk work belongs on the cheapest model, with the dearer ones kept for final renders.


### SiliconFlow embedding, reranking, and dedicated GPU pricing


When a retrieval pipeline makes many embedding and rerank calls per query, those charge on input. Cost the whole pipeline, not the generation step alone, and check each model's unit before comparing it with a chat model.

Billed for time, not tokens, dedicated and reserved GPUs only beat per-token billing if your traffic keeps the GPU busy. Divide the hourly rate by the tokens you actually push through it to get a comparable per-million figure.
